newsitem.title: USA: N.Y.C. Mayor says city will sue tobacco companies.
newsitem.headline: N.Y.C. Mayor says city will sue tobacco companies.

text.p: New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani said Thursday he planned to announce a lawsuit against major U.S. tobacco companies at a news conference at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT.

Few details about the city's lawsuit were immediately available. In a brief statement, the city said that it will seek to recover the costs of treating lung cancer and other tobacco-related diseases in Medicaid patients and uninsured patients treated without charge in public hospitals.
The statement added that New York City also will try to recover the medical expenses incurred by its employees.
"The complaint also seeks reimbursement for the tobacco-related costs of providing health benefits to city employees," it said.

The Coalition for a Smoke-Free City, which has been urging the mayor to file suit due to inaction by New York State Attorney General Dennis Vacco, said earlier that the city was expected to announce the tobacco lawsuit this afternoon.
A spokesman for the state attorney general had no immediate comment on the announcement by New York City.
New York City's lawsuit is expected to resemble those brought by 16 states that also are attempting to recoup health care costs of smokers.
